Casa Lapostolle

Clos Apalta

RedDesignation of Origin (zone within the Rapel Valley) Colchagua Valley

Casa Lapostolle’s grand vin, a Carmenère-based blend from old vines in Apalta, in the Colchagua Valley, whose first vintage was 1997.

Clos Apalta is Casa Lapostolle’s emblematic wine and one of Chile’s best-known reds internationally. It was born with the 1997 vintage, from old vines on the Apalta estate in the Colchagua Valley, planted on granitic hillsides within the amphitheatre formed by the area’s hills.

The blend is based on Carmenère, accompanied by Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon and, in some vintages, other varieties, in proportions that vary with the harvest. Winemaking is meticulous: the grapes are hand-picked and also destemmed by hand, berry by berry, before fermentation. The wine is made at the Apalta winery, built on several levels dug into the hillside to work by gravity, and aged in French oak barrels in its underground cellar. The vineyard is farmed according to organic and biodynamic principles. The result is a red of great concentration and complexity, with ripe black fruit, spice and herbal notes, a dense texture and fine tannins, made for long ageing.

Tasting profile

Very deep purple-red. Blackberry, cassis, plum, sweet spice, pepper and herbs. Dense, velvety palate with fine tannins and a very persistent finish.

Food pairing

Roast lamb, game, beef stews, aged cheeses

Serving

17-18 °C, decanted, large glass
